verdict.rationale: Weave's first-party docs describe custom code-based scorers in two forms: function-based scorers (Python functions decorated with @weave.op) and class-based scorers that inherit from weave.Scorer. Scorers return a dictionary of metrics, and the Evaluation object takes one or more scoring functions. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of custom scorer authoring, and documentation of how custom metrics are aggregated (e.g. a custom summarize).

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can write custom code-based scorers and metrics for my evaluations

citations.quote: Function-based Scorers: Python functions decorated with @weave.op. Class-based Scorers: Python classes that inherit from weave.Scorer for more complex evaluations.
Custom Scorers let you encode evaluation criteria that are specific to your use case, beyond what the built-in Scorers cover.
In Weave, Scorers evaluate AI outputs and return evaluation metrics. They take the AI’s output, analyze it, and return a dictionary of results.
